### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f7e836da1ed344aaa6936b9de8b173d0f326b9ec`.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f7e836da1ed344aaa6936b9de8b173d0f326b9ec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b1ddbcb2ecb386c8e36ad8e6da4f79d6b3223331` — the merge of head `ef94551925f2cdf22a074003509ee81e42efd6ab` into base `f7e836da1ed344aaa6936b9de8b173d0f326b9ec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b1ddbcb2ecb386c8e36ad8e6da4f79d6b3223331 && git checkout b1ddbcb2ecb386c8e36ad8e6da4f79d6b3223331
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f7e836da1ed344aaa6936b9de8b173d0f326b9ec ef94551925f2cdf22a074003509ee81e42efd6ab && git checkout -B drift-repro f7e836da1ed344aaa6936b9de8b173d0f326b9ec && git merge --no-ff ef94551925f2cdf22a074003509ee81e42efd6ab

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f7e836da1ed344aaa6936b9de8b173d0f326b9ec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f7e836da1ed344aaa6936b9de8b173d0f326b9ec` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4274c652f7bfeff1c33f7f73ac97370f4f5f8d24`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23809 (body, the dispatch claim 6209728672 and the os-dev-report 6211151563), PR #23846 (body, its 29-file list, the net diff against `main` at `3fed1eb00af6520f1f26e774195b0819d94fb254`), and the head's check-runs. Face: published schema (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`, `object.zod.ts`, `ui/view.zod.ts`); no governed path in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green); 558 / 27 lines.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. `SelectOptionSchema` gains `kind: z.enum(['open', 'won', 'lost']).optional()`, no default, absent stays absent at parse — RIGHT. Card Target 1 reads an absent kind as the open category (a reading, never a written default) and the maintainer's ruling withholds a default under `stageField`; pinned by `a plain select without kinds parses, and an absent kind stays absent`.
2. The vocabulary `open | won | lost` — RIGHT. `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` on `main` already ships `record:path` `stages[].terminal: z.enum(['won', 'lost'])`, so the data layer and the page say one thing one way, no conversion. The card left the spelling to the spec seat. The dev's premise reading (the objectui renderer honours `terminal` first) is a measurement reported in the PR body, outside this record's inputs and not re-measured here; the spec-side half holds on `main`.
3. `FieldSchema` refuses `kind` at `options.N.kind` on any field that is not a single-value `select` / `radio` (`SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES` on `main` is exactly `select`, `radio`; `multiple: true` excluded) — RIGHT. A lifecycle is one value per record; a key no renderer could read is refused, not parsed (ADR-0049). Not itself an accept-set narrowing: `strictObject` refused the unknown key before. Pinned over seven types.
4. `ObjectSchema` refuses, at parse beside `refuseDishonestReferenceDeletedWhen`, every option of the `stageField` field that lacks `kind`, one located issue per option at `fields.FIELD.options.N.kind` naming the field and the option — RIGHT. This is the card's Target 1 second bullet verbatim and the accept-set NARROWING the Clause-② arm declares; reaches every door (`create()` pinned).
5. `ObjectSchema` refuses at `stageField` a picklist-backed stage field, and a multi-value (`multiselect`, `multiple: true`) stage field that carries options — RIGHT, with a note: both go beyond the card's wording; both are declared in the changeset and in the D3 entry; zero corpus instances (`git grep` of `stageField:` string authors on `main`: the showcase `semantic-zoo` and the metadata-core fixture named under ③). The open questions are answered under ③.
6. The three unchanged postures — `stageField: false`, a pointer to an undeclared field (lint `semantic-roles` owns it), a field with no option source — RIGHT as implemented and as pinned (`leaves the existing postures alone`).
7. **The `stageField` `.describe()` — WRONG.** The new sentence reads: "The named field is a single-value `select` / `radio` with inline `options`, and every option declares its `kind` ('open' / 'won' / 'lost'); refused otherwise." The parse does not refuse "otherwise": a `stageField` naming a `text` field, or a `select` with neither `options` nor `picklist`, parses — item 6, which the function docblock calls "unchanged, on purpose" and the PR's own pin asserts (`ObjectSchema.safeParse(lead({ type: 'text' })).success` is `true`). That describe is the JSON-schema description every AI author reads, regenerated into `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` in this very diff, and it advertises a refusal the runtime does not deliver — Prime Directive #10, "keep the claim as narrow as the enforcement". Fix: narrow the sentence to what `refuseStageFieldWithoutKinds` enforces (a stage field that carries options is refused unless it is a single-value `select` / `radio` with inline `options` each declaring `kind`; a picklist-backed one is refused; `false`, an unresolved pointer and an option-less field are left to lint and the heuristics), then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` and `check:generated --fix` so `object.mdx` and whatever else reports stale move with it.
8. Exported type `SelectOptionKind` (api-surface and export-origins, one row each); no `SelectOptionKindSchema` export — RIGHT. The dev measured that a schema export rewrote five `skills/**/references/_index.md` files (Tier H governed, outside the card) and stopped; the type carries the three literals a consumer needs. A runtime-enum export, if a consumer ever needs one, is its own card.
9. `FormSelectOptionSchema` (`view.zod.ts`) now omits `kind` as well as `default`, with guidance pointing at the object field — RIGHT. It is derived structurally from `SelectOptionSchema.shape`, so without the omit `kind` would have parsed on form-view options with no reader. Outside the claim's listed surface but forced by the derivation, and not a ⛔ path (`component.zod.ts` is untouched). Pinned in `form-select-option.test.ts`.
10. `PicklistSchema` options accept `kind` (the option shape is reused verbatim on `main`) — RIGHT as a consequence; the picklist ledger row `options.kind: planned` records that nothing reads it and that no stage use exists (item 5 refuses it).
11. Forms: the `object.form.ts` repeater offers `kind` as a three-value select with help text, `field.form.ts` lists it, and the `en` / `zh-CN` / `ja-JP` / `es-ES` metadata-form bundles are regenerated and translated — RIGHT. The repeater is also shown for multi-value types where the door refuses `kind`: loud at publish (a located issue) and the help text scopes it; acceptable as noted, not an authoring trap.
12. Liveness: `field/options` drilled (six children `live` with read points, `kind` graded `planned` without `authorWarn`), the debt row leaves `undrilled-containers.baseline.json`, the state-counts move — RIGHT. `planned` is the honest grade: the refusals are live at parse, the value is read by nothing until the objectui follow-up (card Target 4; Constraints: the spec declares before any consumer reads). No `authorWarn` is right: the author-side lint would warn on every compliant stage field, where the key is mandatory. `Spec property liveness` is green.
13. D3 entry `18.stage-field-option-kind-required.ts` (surface, replacement, reason, acceptanceCriteria; no `conversionIds`) under the open protocol major 18 (`PROTOCOL_VERSION` 18.0.0) — RIGHT. No D2 conversion is correct: the ruling withholds a default, so no lossless mechanical edit exists, and ADR-0087 sends a non-convertible break to D3. The registry is generated and gitignored, nothing to commit; the step-18 rationale is a fragment list that no gate pairs to entries (123 fragments against 387 entries on `main`), so no fragment is owed.
14. Showcase `semantic-zoo.object.ts` options declare `open` / `open` / `won` — RIGHT (the one `stageField: 'status'` in the corpus; `SemanticZooLegacy` is `stageField: false`, untouched by the rule).
15. Reference docs (`content/docs/references/**`, six files) regenerated by `gen:docs` — a prose face outside this review; named only because item 7's fix moves `object.mdx` again.

Check-runs on the head, read last at 2026-10-16T08:41Z: 33 success, 5 skipped (the full-battery jobs a PR run does not carry), 2 still in progress — `Test Core (3/6)` and `Test Core (4/6)`. Green: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · workspace` / `source gates` / `consumer gates` / `debt ledger`, `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/6, 2/6, 5/6, 6/6)`, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. The two shards are named as in progress rather than waited on; no landing before they conclude green.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23809-select-option-kind.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, summary `feat(spec)!: …`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, a FROM → TO migration with the one-line fix, and the adr-0087 `registered stage-field-option-kind-required` marker — level, arm and disposition are RIGHT. `yes`: the option shape widens by a new authorable key, at least `minor`. `(narrowing)`: `ObjectSchema`'s accept set shrinks (items 4 and 5), BREAKING, and it carries its migration and its ADR-0087 marker as the Post-Task Checklist demands. `minor`, not `major`: the launch-window convention in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` ships a breaking change as `minor` in the lockstep fixed group until GA, and `.changeset/pre.json` is in `pre` mode (tag `next`). The PR body's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` agrees with the changeset; the claim's bare `Clause-②: yes` predates the measured shape, and the arm is the dev's correct refinement (③).
- **Package set — WRONG.** The diff publishes a changed `@objectstack/platform-objects`: the four `src/apps/translations/*.metadata-forms.generated.ts` bundles gain the `fields.options.kind` and `options.kind` rows, and they are reached from the published `./metadata-translations` entry (`src/metadata-translations/index.ts`, a tsup entry, `files: dist`). The changeset names `@objectstack/spec` alone. "Add a changeset for anything that publishes" — and every one of the last six landings on `main` that moved `en.metadata-forms.generated.ts` names `'@objectstack/platform-objects'` (changesets 23808, 23735, 23543, 23488, 23395 and 15204-s8: `patch` or `minor`). The fixed group bumps it either way; what is missing is its CHANGELOG line, the text an upgrading agent greps. Fix: add `'@objectstack/platform-objects': patch` to the changeset frontmatter (the dev's own report lists the bundles under `files_changed`). `Check Changeset` is green on this head, so this is not something CI catches here.
- Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the published option shape widens and `ObjectSchema`'s accept set narrows.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's `deviations` and `open_questions` on the os-dev-report, each answered or escalated:

- OQ1, a picklist-backed stage field refused at parse (A) or judged on the resolved list (B): **A, accepted.** The parse is the one door every save passes; B would judge only the CLI doors and let the save door through unjudged (declared ≠ enforced). Zero corpus instances; widening to B later is non-breaking; the narrowing is declared in the changeset and the D3 entry (item 5). Not escalated.
- OQ2, a multi-value stage field carrying options refused at `stageField`: **A, accepted.** A record stands at one stage; without it `multiple: true` would slip the mandatory-kind rule silently. Zero corpus instances; declared in the changeset and the D3 entry. Not escalated.
- Files beyond the claim's surface (`view.zod.ts` and its pin, `liveness/picklist.json`, `undrilled-containers.baseline.json`, `field-rows-option-description.test.ts`, the platform-objects bundles, the D3 entry): each forced by a measurement the dev names; none touches a ⛔ path of the claim (`component.zod.ts`, `skills/**`, `content/docs/releases/**`, objectui and HotCRM are all untouched). Accepted; the platform-objects bundles are what ② charges to the changeset.
- No `SelectOptionKindSchema` export: right to stop (item 8); the governed `skills/**` rewrite was outside the card.
- The `(narrowing)` arm added where the claim read a bare `yes`: right (②).
- A worktree created on the pre-existing branch, one vitest run outside `os-verify-lock`, no label-write: process flags outside the contract faces; noted, nothing to answer here.
- out_of_scope_findings 1, the options repeater offering `kind` on multi-value types: accepted as noted (item 11); loud at publish, not a trap.
- out_of_scope_findings 2 — **escalated to the owning seat.** `FLS_CONTRACT_OBJECT` in `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-contract.ts`, exported from the published `@objectstack/metadata-core/testing`, declares `stageField: 'salary_grade'` over two kind-less select options. No door in its suites parses it through `ObjectSchema` (the dev's rest, runtime and metadata-core runs are green), so nothing is red — but a published contract fixture now fails `ObjectSchema.parse` under the spec it ships beside, a trap for the next consumer that feeds it to a parsing door. Two answers, either acceptable: add `kind: 'open'` to its two options on the push item 7 already demands (two lines outside the claim surface, so say so in the PR body), or file a card naming the trap. This record does not choose between them.
- On `main`, the only `stageField` string authors outside tests are `semantic-zoo` and that fixture; lint's `stageField: 'status'` fixtures run `validateSemanticRoles` on raw stacks and never through `ObjectSchema`, so the in-progress `Test Core` shards carry no known red from this rule.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23809-select-option-kind`
Reviewed-by: `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Two edits re-earn a PASS on a new head: ① item 7 (narrow the `stageField` describe and regenerate) and ② (add `'@objectstack/platform-objects': patch`); ③'s fixture escalation is the seat's choice of an in-PR edit or a card. Everything else on the three faces is right.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `447546949874cd7706decaac1833b07c21b2ecbc`
Local-runs: none

DELTA record on contract review 6211666660 (FAIL at `4274c652f7bfeff1c33f7f73ac97370f4f5f8d24`). Inputs: card #23809 (body, the dispatch claim 6209728672, the os-dev-reports 6211151563 and 6212681414), PR #23846 (body, its 34-file list, the docs-drift comment 6211145627, the prior record, and the net diff against `main` at `3fed1eb00af6520f1f26e774195b0819d94fb254`, merge-base `1ecb08a1cc`), and the head's check-runs. The delta `git diff 4274c652 44754694` is three commits over 10 files, +63 / -14: the `stageField` TSDoc and `.describe()` in `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (the function body of `refuseStageFieldWithoutKinds` is untouched), the changeset frontmatter and one new body paragraph, the metadata-core fixture and a new pin, three platform-objects count pins, and three regenerated reference pages. Face: published schema in the file list; no governed path (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green on the head).

### ① Derived judgments

Items 1 to 6 and 8 to 15 of record 6211666660 stand unchanged: the delta does not touch `field.zod.ts`, `ui/view.zod.ts`, the two forms, the liveness ledgers, the D3 entry, the showcase object, or the refusal function's code. Judged on this head:

- **Item 7, prior FAIL ground (1) — CLOSED.** The new `stageField` describe reads: "When the named field carries options, it must be a single-value `select` / `radio` with inline `options`, each declaring its `kind` ('open' / 'won' / 'lost'); a picklist-backed or multi-value stage field is refused. A name that resolves to no declared field, or a field with no options, is not judged at parse." Read clause by clause against `refuseStageFieldWithoutKinds` on the head: a non-string `stageField` or a name absent from `fields` returns without an issue; a type outside `SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES` (exactly `select`, `radio` on the head) or `multiple: true` is refused at `stageField` only when the field carries `options` or `picklist`, and returns otherwise (so `stageField: 'a_text_field'` still parses, as the PR's own pin asserts); a single-value field with `picklist` and no `options` is refused at `stageField`; an `options` array raises one located issue per option lacking `kind`. `FieldSchema` refuses `options` and `picklist` together ("a field takes its options from exactly one source"), so no coexistence edge lets a picklist-backed stage field through the options branch. The claim is now exactly as wide as the enforcement (Prime Directive #10). The `[#23809]` TSDoc above it says the same, and the describe is regenerated into `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`, `api/metadata.mdx` and `system/migration.mdx` (two tables); `Type Check · source gates`, the job that runs `check:authorable-surface` and `check:docs`, is green on the head.
- **Item 16 (new): `FLS_CONTRACT_OBJECT` in `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-contract.ts` declares `kind: 'open'` on both `salary_grade` options — RIGHT.** The fixture is published: `src/testing.ts` re-exports the module and `package.json` serves `./testing` from `dist`. `open` on both is the right reading (a salary band is a step, never an end). It is pinned in `object-schema-fls-references.test.ts` by a block that collects `ObjectSchema.safeParse` issues at `stageField` or under `fields.salary_grade.options`, asserts none, and has a positive control that strips one `kind` and asserts exactly `fields.salary_grade.options.1.kind`. The pin's scope is honest and necessary: the fixture is deliberately not a whole-object valid document — its four `script` actions carry neither `body` nor `target` nor `operation: 'update'`, which `ActionSchema` refuses at `actions.N.body` ("A 'script' action requires either an inline `body` ... or a `target`"), and the pin's comment says so. Prior ③ escalation closed by the in-PR edit.
- **Item 17 (new): the three platform-objects count pins — RIGHT as read against the bundles.** `field-panel-echo-decisions` `ROW_PROPERTIES` 10 to 11 is the field form's `options.kind` row; `object-collapsed-sections-echo-decisions` `OPEN_LEAVES` 116 to 118 is the object form's `fields.options.kind` label plus its help text; `object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions` 672 to 674 per locale is one row label on each form. All four bundles (`en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`) carry both keys with the same shape. Test-side pins only; the dev names `Test Core (3/6)` as the shard that was red on the intermediate head `ec9f775f` for exactly these three counts, and that shard judges them on this head (below).

Check-runs on the head, read last at 2026-10-16T09:59Z: 37 success, 7 skipped (the full-battery jobs a PR run does not carry, plus the `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` duplicates of the 09:54Z re-trigger), 3 still in progress: `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)`. Green: `Lint & Repo Gates` and every `Lint ·` job, `Type Check · workspace` / `source gates` / `consumer gates` / `debt ledger`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Test Core (1/6, 2/6, 5/6)`, `Check Changeset` (both runs), `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the four card-claim guards. The three shards are named as in progress rather than waited on; no landing before they conclude green, and `(3/6)` is the one that carries the count pins.

### ② Semver level

- Level, arm and disposition unchanged from the prior record and still RIGHT: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `feat(spec)!:` summary, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, the FROM → TO migration with the one-line fix, the `adr-0087: registered stage-field-option-kind-required` marker; `.changeset/pre.json` in `pre` mode, the launch-window `minor` for a breaking change in the fixed group. `Check Changeset` green twice on the head. The PR body's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` agrees.
- **Package set, prior FAIL ground (2) — CLOSED.** The frontmatter now carries `'@objectstack/platform-objects': patch` (the `./metadata-translations` bundles gain the two `kind` rows) and `'@objectstack/metadata-core': patch` (the `./testing` fixture), each with its own sentence in the body. `patch` is right for both: a bundle row and a fixture value, no API widening; the fixed group bumps them either way and what was missing was the CHANGELOG line.
- **One clause of the new metadata-core sentence is WRONG, and it is the reason for the verdict.** The body reads: "The published contract fixture `FLS_CONTRACT_OBJECT` (`@objectstack/metadata-core/testing`) names `salary_grade` as its `stageField`, so its two options now declare `kind: 'open'` and the fixture still parses through `ObjectSchema`." It does not, and it never did: `ActionSchema` refuses each of the fixture's four `script` actions at `actions.N.body` (no `body`, no `target`, no `operation: 'update'`), so `ObjectSchema.safeParse(FLS_CONTRACT_OBJECT).success` is `false` on this head. The dev measured exactly that (report 6212681414: "its script actions carry no body/target, measured: actions.0.body / actions.1.body issues") and scoped the pin to the stage-field rule for that reason; the pin's own comment says "The fixture is not a whole spec-valid object". The changeset body is the text `changeset version` compiles into `packages/metadata-core/CHANGELOG.md`, shipped inside the npm tarball as what an upgrading agent greps (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3 and the Documentation Guardrails row for `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md`: a factual error in a released entry is correctable only in a later docs-only PR the reader never reaches). This sentence tells that agent the fixture is safe to feed to a parsing door, which is the trap record 6211666660 escalated under ③, now advertised as absent. Same class as prior ground (1): a claim wider than what the runtime delivers (Prime Directive #10). Fix, one line and no regeneration: replace "and the fixture still parses through `ObjectSchema`" with what the pin asserts, for example "and `ObjectSchema` raises no stage-field issue on it (the fixture is not a whole spec-valid object by design: its `script` actions carry no `body` or `target`)", or delete the clause.
- Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the published option shape widens and `ObjectSchema`'s accept set narrows; unchanged by the delta.

### ③ Boundary flags

The round-2 os-dev-report 6212681414 carries `open_questions: []` and `out_of_scope_findings: []`; its `deviations`, each answered:
